headline: One Day, £12m Given Away: How a Firm Turned Tragedy into Purpose
meta_description: BGC Group donates 100% of a day's revenue to charity, raising £12m this year. A 25-year tradition born from 9/11 that's changing lives.
summary_short: On September 11, BGC Group gives away an entire day's revenue to charity. This year, with help from celebrities like Jamie Redknapp, they raised £12m.
body:
Every September 11, the trading floor at BGC Group in Canary Wharf transforms into something unusual: a place where making money becomes an act of generosity. This year, celebrities including Jamie Redknapp, Dame Helen Mirren, and Tom Hardy took to the phones, closing trades worth tens of millions of pounds. But here's what made it different from any ordinary trading day—100% of the revenue from those deals went directly to charity. By day's end, BGC had raised US$16 million (£12 million) for organisations across the UK and beyond. Since launching this annual tradition in 2005, the firm has donated a global total of US$250 million.

The practice was born from unimaginable loss. On September 11, 2001, BGC's parent company, Cantor Fitzgerald, lost 658 employees—more than any other organisation. Co-CEO Sean Windeatt, then 28, was working in London when the phone call with his New York counterpart went dead mid-conversation. After saving the company through those impossible first months, leadership decided that once families of the deceased were supported, they would dedicate one full day each year to raising money for global charities.

For the organisations that receive this funding, the impact is profound and measurable. Debbi Clark, founder of HvH Arts, a London-based charity serving marginalised children, explains that BGC's donation now represents one-third of her annual income—money that has allowed her to treble the number of children they help since 2019. For 12-year-old Carmela Chillery-Watson, who has a rare form of muscular dystrophy, BGC's funding enabled Muscular Dystrophy UK to provide the custom wheelchair she uses every day—equipment the NHS doesn't cover. Her mother Lucy voiced what many feel: "I wish more companies did things like this." New research shows only 27% of UK businesses support charities, and corporate giving has halved as a percentage of profits since 2009. BGC's example suggests another path is possible.
quick_facts: BGC raised £12 million on September 11, 2024 charity day
100% of revenue—not just profits—went to charities that day
Founded after Cantor Fitzgerald lost 658 staff in 9/11
Celebrities including Jamie Redknapp helped close trades
